name: GOLD STAR
tagline: 1970 MIT Project MAC thesis system that managed data as set-theoretic relations on Multics.
description: GOLD STAR was a data management system described in Andrew Fillat and Leslie Kraning's June 1970 MIT thesis, published as Project MAC technical report TR-70, "Generalized Organization of Large Data-Bases; A Set-Theoretic Approach to Relations". It modelled a database as sets and relations between data elements and offered union, intersection, difference, composition, projection, Cartesian product and sorting as primitive operations, implemented in PL/I on Multics with separate managers for data sets and relations. It appeared the same year as Codd's relational model paper and reached similar set-based conclusions independently. It never left the lab, but it is an early example of treating data management as algebra over relations rather than navigation through records.
statusNote: Research prototype from a 1970 MIT thesis (Project MAC TR-70); never released as a product.
developer: MIT Project MAC (Andrew Fillat, Leslie Kraning)

pricing.notes: Never distributed; the source listing is printed in the technical report.

strengths: Early, independent set-theoretic treatment of relations (1970)
Relational operators such as project, compose and Cartesian product as primitives
Full PL/I source and design rationale printed in the report
weaknesses: Thesis prototype never used in production
useCases: Comparing pre-SQL approaches to relational data
